editorial:
You follow Malcolm, a smart kid from Inglewood who loves 90s hip-hop and is trying to get into Harvard. A chance party invitation goes wrong, and he ends up with a backpack full of drugs he never asked for. The vibe is energetic, funny, and heartfelt, mixing coming-of-age charm with real street tension. You will root for Malcolm and his two best friends as they scramble to fix the mess without losing their future.

The acting is strong, especially Shameik Moore, who makes Malcolm feel real and lovable. The pacing moves fast, with sharp humor and a great soundtrack. Some plot twists feel a bit convenient, and the tone shifts can be jarring. Still, it is a fun, feel-good ride. If you like clever teen comedies with heart, this is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Malcolm realizes the drug deal was a setup by a local dealer who wanted to use him. Instead of getting arrested, Malcolm uses his smarts to outsmart everyone, selling the drugs online and using the money to fund his Harvard application. He writes his college essay about the experience, turning his chaos into a story of survival. The twist is that the whole mess actually helps him become himself and earn his spot at Harvard.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age comedies with heart and a great soundtrack.
